title: Elements to improve AI-advice identified
full_text:
The Actuaries Institute has outlined four practical areas it believes would help create better artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled financial advice following a review of how popular chatbots handle Australian retirement and investment scenarios.
These aspects include improving financial literacy, encouraging AI-enabled innovation in Australian financial services, modernising regulation and strengthening regulatory supervision of AI-enabled financial services.
All are discussed in the professional body’s paper, “How AI can help people make better financial decisions: Improving access to financial help, guidance and advice”.
In developing the analysis, the authors tested four popular chatbots using five hypothetical retirement and investment scenarios.
“What is most concerning is that all four failed the most consequential question in our testing – a detailed query about retirement advice – at a time when one in eight over-45s use AI for super and retirement questions,” Actuaries Institute public policy council committee member and actuary Nathan Bonarius said.
Given the fall in adviser numbers since 2018 to about 15,000, chatbots may seem like an easy option for many Australians unable to afford or access appropriate financial advice. But Bonarius indicated most people lack the financial experience and expertise to ask the appropriate questions of chatbots in the right way.
During their research, the authors found many popular chatbots and existing AI-enabled advice models struggled to perform calculations, projections and scenario modellings. It was also difficult to explain and audit their responses.
“AI has the potential to democratise access to high-quality financial advice. However, you need to be able to trust it and that relies on AI being well regulated, controlled and governed,” Bonarius noted.
According to the Actuaries Institute, the industry needs to work together to create the right environment to develop AI-enabled financial advice models that can provide meaningful solutions for more Australians.
“Actuaries can help support innovation and build trust by designing and testing AI-enabled advice, drawing on their expertise in modelling, risk and governance, with a focus on good outcomes for consumers,” institute chief executive Elayne Grace noted.
